prediction_question: For an aviation occurrence reported to the ATSB, given what was known at notification (occurrence date/time, occurrence type, aircraft category/make, operation type, location), will the ATSB classify it as an accident or serious incident rather than an incident?
prediction_time: At occurrence notification to the ATSB, using only fields documented as recorded at or before notification. Investigation findings and post-hoc classifications would have been excluded as label sources.
target_definition: Binary severity class (accident/serious incident vs incident) from the ATSB occurrence category taxonomy. Label source column: the occurrence severity/classification field, excluded from features.

rejection_reason: Access-blocked under the publisher's own terms: the ATSB refuses whole-database export (200-row cap per dashboard export) and states the database is 'made available for general statistical purposes only', disclaiming use beyond that and declining to endorse commercial use. Constructing a benchmark panel of tens of thousands of occurrences is not possible through the public channel, and a published derived dataset would both exceed the stated purpose limitation and constitute the bulk redistribution the export cap is designed to prevent. No open licence instrument was read because access already vetoes.
review: Triage-first order worked: two page reads (search snippets, then first-hand page fetch) closed the lead with no schema or volume probing spent. The ATSB's own limitation notes ('data may be missing, incomplete', weeks of ingestion lag) would also have complicated any timing claim.
next_action: None - closed. Reopens only if the ATSB publishes a bulk occurrence extract under an open licence (e.g. on data.gov.au with CC BY), which would re-vet as a new source.
licence_note: no open licence instrument found/read; access channel itself refuses bulk export and the publisher limits use to 'general statistical purposes'. Closed under the standing policy without an enquiry.
